lead_headline: Claude Code's Desktop wrapper shows a process lifecycle fault as surface rendering issues accumulate
lead_body: Eight issues landed in Claude Code across the day, most of them rendering pathologies in the terminal and chat panel. The structurally notable one is a Desktop-only exit 143 on cycles past five minutes — the bare CLI runs clean on the same binary, pointing the fault at the Desktop wrapper's process lifecycle. Astro contributed a single Vite optimizeDeps race condition in dev mode; everything else stayed dark.
lead_article:
A quiet Sunday by the numbers, though Claude Code accumulated enough friction to warrant a look. Eight issues opened across the day, most of them surface-layer rendering pathologies: the terminal corruption in VS Code forcing a partial re-render on text selection, the Unicode-mangled chat panel mid-session, the Agent View scroll breakage on Ghostty and Warp under macOS. The more structurally interesting one is the Desktop-only exit 143 — a SIGTERM on cycles past roughly five minutes, while the bare CLI runs clean on identical binary and context. That asymmetry points somewhere specific in the Desktop wrapper's process lifecycle rather than the model or the core. The domain allowlist issue in the sandbox proxy and the Android remote approval failing to unblock the local TUI both suggest the permission and IPC plumbing has some rough edges worth watching as a cluster. On the positive side, the segfault closed out.

Astro had a single report land in the afternoon: a Vite optimizeDeps race condition dropping React in dev mode. One issue, probably reproducible, the kind of thing that bites people during cold starts. Everything else across the board — Hydrogen, Metaflow, Mantis, AI SDK, Workflow SDK, Gemma.cpp, Dispatch Weekly — stayed dark.
